description: Fringe search finds a cheapest path with an *admissible* heuristic `h` (one that never overestimates), like A*, but it needs no priority queue. Like IDA*, it works in iterations with a cost threshold: it expands the states with `f = g + h` up to the threshold, defers the others, and then raises the threshold to the smallest deferred `f`. The *fringe* is two lists, *now* and *later*, and each new or improved successor goes to the head of *now*, so an iteration runs depth-first. Like A*, it caches the best `g` and the parent of every state seen, so it expands a state again only after it finds a cheaper path to it. Use it on grid and game maps with few distinct `f` values; many distinct float costs mean many iterations, and memory grows as for A*.

papers.authors: Yngvi Björnsson, Markus Enzenberger, Robert C. Holte, Jonathan Schaeffer
papers.title: Fringe Search: Beating A* at Pathfinding on Game Maps
papers.venue: IEEE Symposium on Computational Intelligence and Games (CIG)
